scenario: Thorin (Fighter 5, STR 16, Great Weapon Fighting fighting style, 2024 rules) hits a bandit (AC 12, 11 HP) with a greatsword. The damage dice come up 1 and 5.
action: Thorin hits the bandit with his greatsword. Resolve the damage.
notes: 2024 GWF treats any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3: (3 + 5) + 3 STR = 11.

scenario: Brynn (Paladin 4, STR 17, Great Weapon Fighting, 2014 rules) hits an orc (AC 13, 15 HP) with a greatsword. The damage dice come up 2 and 6; the reroll of the 2 comes up 1.
action: Brynn hits the orc with her greatsword. Resolve the damage.
notes: 2014 GWF rerolls a 1 or 2 once and must keep the new roll: 1 + 6 + 3 STR = 10.

scenario: Thorin (Fighter 5, STR 16) has the Graze weapon mastery property with his greatsword. He attacks a hobgoblin (AC 18) and the attack roll total is 14.
action: Thorin swings his greatsword at the hobgoblin. Resolve the attack.
notes: Graze: on a miss the target takes damage equal to the ability modifier used for the attack (+3), of the weapon's damage type.

scenario: Vex (Rogue 3, DEX 16) attacks a goblin with a shortsword (finesse). Thorin, conscious and hostile to the goblin, stands within 5 feet of it. Vex has neither advantage nor disadvantage. The attack hits.
action: Vex stabs the goblin while Thorin keeps it busy. Is Sneak Attack applied?
notes: An ally within 5 ft of the target who isn't incapacitated enables Sneak Attack (2d6 at level 3) with a finesse weapon, absent disadvantage.

scenario: Vex (Rogue 3, STR 14, DEX 16) attacks a goblin with a greataxe (heavy, not finesse) and has advantage on the attack. The attack hits.
action: Vex cleaves the goblin with a greataxe. Is Sneak Attack applied?
notes: Sneak Attack requires a finesse or ranged weapon.

scenario: Vex (Rogue 3, DEX 16) attacks a goblin with a shortbow while blinded by a Darkness spell, so the attack has disadvantage. Thorin stands within 5 feet of the goblin. The attack still hits.
action: Vex fires into the dark at the goblin. Is Sneak Attack applied?
notes: Sneak Attack can't be used when the attack roll has disadvantage, even if an ally is adjacent.

scenario: A hobgoblin (Martial Advantage: once per turn, +2d6 damage to a creature it hits with a weapon attack if that creature is within 5 ft of an ally of the hobgoblin that isn't incapacitated) hits Thorin with its longsword. A second hobgoblin, conscious and unrestrained, stands within 5 feet of Thorin. Longsword damage 1d8+1 comes up 6; Martial Advantage 2d6 comes up 3 and 4.
action: The hobgoblin hits Thorin. Resolve the damage.

scenario: A hobgoblin hits Thorin with its longsword for 5 damage. The only other hobgoblin near Thorin is unconscious (incapacitated) at 0 HP within 5 feet of him.
action: The hobgoblin hits Thorin. Does Martial Advantage add damage?
notes: Martial Advantage needs an ally that isn't incapacitated.

scenario: Round 1 of combat. The party ambushed a sleeping-watch bandit, who is surprised and has not yet taken its first turn. Vex moves out of the bandit's reach before the bandit's turn.
action: Can the surprised bandit make an opportunity attack against Vex?
notes: 2014: a surprised creature can't take reactions until its first turn ends.

scenario: Using 2024 rules, the party ambushes three cultists who fail to notice them. Initiative is about to be rolled.
action: What does surprise do to the cultists? Do they lose their first turn?
notes: 2024: surprised creatures have disadvantage on the initiative roll; they do not lose a turn.

scenario: Caelith (Wizard 3, STR 8) tries to force open an adamantine vault door (Strength (Athletics) DC 25). The d20 shows a natural 20; Caelith has no proficiency in Athletics.
action: Caelith throws her shoulder against the vault door.
notes: A natural 20 is not an automatic success on ability checks: 20 - 1 = 19 < 25.
